decisions.reason: Organic sliced ham fits the firm’s core chilled deli range and its stated push to expand organic products, so a large established producer would usually keep it unless sales clearly disappoint.
Bio Kasseler is still close to the company’s established competence in cured pork and supports the organic line, though it is a slightly narrower everyday use case than ham.
Organic pepper salami combines a familiar salami format with an established flavor profile, making it a strong fit for the firm’s premium self-service assortment.

The teriyaki aspic beef item looks like a more experimental deli-counter specialty and is the kind of niche seasonal innovation a traditional meat producer is most likely to withdraw to simplify the range.
Fennel-flavoured sliced salami is somewhat more niche in taste, but it remains close enough to the firm’s salami business that management would likely keep it while monitoring turnover.
Liver pâté with veal fits the company’s premium pâté offer and craftsmanship positioning, so it is more likely to stay than to be discontinued.
